items.title: doc(id): state the #4592 replication admission contract in replication.rs (#4593)
items.body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #4592, for issue #4593 (task 14247).

## What

- States the #4592 admission contract verbatim in the pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs module doc (new 'Admission contract (#4592)' section): a frame is admitted only if its header version names a chain that could exist — inside the restore range JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION, and, for a snapshot, never lower than the version of the chain the tracker already holds.
- Cross-references the contract from the ReplicationTracker::accept doc comment.
- Documentation only; no behavior change.

## Audit outcome (full inventory posted on issue #4593)

Every WorldCore::restore precondition was dispositioned against accept at origin/main 1cd22df899. Header presence/shape, header world, header version range, per-entry decodability, and payload header agreement (#4486) all hold at accept. Dispositions (b), (c), (d) confirmed with code/test evidence on issue #4593. One confirmed gap: per-entry version requirements (disposition (a)) are enforced at restore (core.rs) but not at accept — filed as follow-up issue #7970, not fixed here per the audit scope.

## Tests

- cargo test -p id --lib world::replication on the laptop (result recorded on issue #4593 / task 14247).

items.title: feat(id-core): existence acknowledgements bound to the B19 receipt schema (#10256)
items.body: ## What Lands slice A9115-existence-receipt for #10256: existence acknowledgements bound to the shared B19 V2 receipt schema, as two new files in `id-core`: - `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/existence_receipt.rs` — `ExistsAck`, the #9115 consumer binding of a B19 `verified_present` receipt. Canonical bytes are B19's byte for byte (same domain, field order, kind tag), so an ack here is a B19 `verified_present` receipt on the wire; the ack reader refuses `accepted`/`retained_until` receipts as `WrongAssertion` and unknown tags as `UnknownAssertion`. It binds responder identity + key, subject digest, tenant/namespace scope, policy epoch + digest, and observation time, plus the B19 challenge/response presence proof (`check_presence`). `verify` runs the interval + signature gate and returns a `VerifiedAck` exposing responder/scope/epoch for the consuming authority gate. `stored_unverified` is a distinct unsigned `StoredUnverifiedObservation` that never proves presence; `NotPresent` and `Indeterminate` are distinct internal `ExistenceResult`s that policy may coalesce via `coalesced()`. - `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/tests/existence_receipt.rs` — the declared model oracle: an independent reference implementation of the documented B19 layout (own byte builder, own presence response, dalek used directly), a pinned golden vector (SHA-256 of the fixed ack's canonical bytes), deterministic coverage of every error class, and two proptests (generated answer/verify round-trips compared against the model; single-byte tamper never verifies). Scope notes: the module is a self-contained leaf, included by path in its test — the crate-root export stays with the wiring slice (9110-02 line), as the neighbouring ID slices do. No existing file is modified. ## Verification `cargo test -p id-core --test existence_receipt` in `nix develop` (pkgs/id): **12 passed / 0 failed**, re-run green after `rustfmt` on both files. No new warnings from the added files. Closes #10256 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(id): design note for #4630 — bound the checkpoint at write time so every entry fits a v1 replication frame
items.body: ## What Design note for #4630: the replication feed cannot send a journal whose compacted `Checkpoint` entry exceeds `MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (256 KiB), because `split_entry_payload` breaks only at entry boundaries. This note chooses the fix mechanism; it implements nothing. ## Decision **Bound the checkpoint at write time** (`core.rs::checkpoint_entries`) by emitting it as bounded part entries (snapshot / retained events / admin history), with `MAX_CHECKPOINT_PART_BYTES = 192 KiB` — deliberately below the existing 256 KiB payload bound. Consequences, spelled out in the note: - no replication wire change, no envelope-version bump, no `ReplicationTracker::accept` change, no receiver upgrade; - `JOURNAL_VERSION` 6 for the new part kinds (older binaries refuse at the header check, as for versions 2–5); - the v1 invariant #4592 relies on — payloads are whole entries, the cursor is entries absorbed — is preserved exactly; - the note states the resulting per-entry guarantee and the one residual case (a `Checkpoint` written by an older binary, not since re-compacted), which gets its own follow-up. Rejected/deferred with reasons: (a) sub-entry fragmentation (v1→v2 wire bump, permanent receiver buffering for a writer-controlled entry kind); (b) larger in-frame allowance (cannot bound an unbounded program snapshot; changes a receiver-side constant, so silently compatibility-splitting). Both are recorded, not hand-waved. ## Tests Doc-only: no code paths change. The note names the checks the implementation issues must run (`cargo test -p id --lib world::replication`, the `world_store` replication feed tests, journal-version/restore tests, and the #4630 oversized-Checkpoint round-trip regression). Closes nothing: #4630 stays open for the implementation. ## Issues - #4630 (design parent, remains open) - Implementation follow-ups filed from this note and linked on #4630. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: impl(deploy): the release verb — tag cutting, attestation, and the untagged-release refusal (#13306)
items.body: Implements the release verb for the deploy tool, per the release-workflow design record (#11177) and issue #13306. **What lands** - `deploy release [--version X.Y.Z] [--commit ] [--bump minor|patch]` — the estate's only release actor. It verifies the commit is reachable from `origin/main`, judges the attestation gate for that exact commit (the main-gate watched set, judged by the same rules `.github/scripts/release-gate.sh` implements — the non-push ancestor rule is the live one — plus the app's own evidence workflow when the watched set does not cover it), checks the ratified #5790 version discipline (short app-name prefix, first tag `0.1.0`, 0.x only, next minor or next patch only, duplicate/collision refusals), cuts the annotated app tag carrying the `release-attestation:v1` block and the release point's annotated `repo/v..` tag, pushes both, and appends the release record to the release ledger (`releases.jsonl` in the deploy state dir). `--dry-run` judges and reports without cutting. - The deploy-time refusal (design §6): a deploy whose artifact self-reports a clean `X.Y.Z` version claims release status and is refused in both activation paths (systemd and sandbox) unless an attested `/vX.Y.Z` tag exists at the artifact's source commit with a verifiable attestation block. Prerelease (`-dev`) artifacts are unaffected. The app a definition speaks for is its name or the app whose binary it runs, so the fleet services verify against `fleet/vX.Y.Z`. - Registry: new optional field `evidenceWorkflow` (design §3 part 2), validated like the other optional fields and set to `fleet-rust-tests` on the fleet-backed definitions (`queue-broker`, `secrets-broker`) in `pkgs/deploy/services.nix`. - `deploy status` (bare) reads the release ledger beside the per-target reports; where ledger and tags disagree the tag wins and the disagreement is reported. Per-target status also lists that app's ledger records. - `pkgs/fleet/README.md`: the tag-and-release procedure now names the design record as the workflow of record. **Verification** - New `pkgs/deploy/test_deploy_release.py` (17 tests) over a fixture git remote with faked `gh`: successful release producing both tags with a parseable attestation block, second/third releases following the discipline and the repo-tag counter, dry-run cutting nothing, red-gate / missing-signal / off-main / version-discipline / unknown-app refusals, the untagged-release deploy refusal (and the attested control deploying), and the ledger round-trip through the status report including tag-wins disagreement. - All nine `pkgs/deploy` suites pass on the laptop; `nix build .#deploy` succeeds and the rendered registry carries `evidenceWorkflow` on both fleet services (verified in the built CLI's registry JSON). - A remote dispatch of the same suites at this head is recorded on #13306. The first real release cut with the verb (`fleet/v0.1.0` plus the repo tag) follows the merge if the gate judges green at cutting time, recorded on #11177 as the acceptance requires; #13306 stays open until that leg is recorded. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(ci-policy checker): verify push branches: [main] for the main tier (#7950)
items.body: Closes #7950. The ci-policy agreement checker (PR #7945, #7089 Phase 1) enforced the main tier by trigger *name* only: any `push` satisfied the leg, though the pinned contract in `.github/ci-policy.md` is a push on `branches: [main]`. A push that can never run on main was certified as agreeing — and for waived workflows flipped to **STALE WAIVER**, ordering the waiver deleted in the same PR (the issue's probe cases 1–4 reproduce exactly this, ending in a false `ci-policy-agreement: OK`). **Fix** (`.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh`): - New `push_targets_main` reads the push trigger's own sub-keys from the workflow's `on:` block — `branches`, `branches-ignore`, `tags` in both flow-list (`branches: [main]`) and block-sequence forms, alongside the existing bare/scalar/flow trigger forms. - The main leg now agrees only when the push actually targets main: bare/unfiltered `push:` still counts; an explicit `branches:` filter must list `main`; `branches-ignore:` naming `main`, a `branches:` list without `main`, and a tags-only push keep the leg in disagreement — reported as WAIVED against its recorded waiver (with a message that names the mis-targeting), or as a DISAGREEMENT when unwaived. Never stale, never certified. - No workflow triggers, tiers, or waivers change; the named-equivalent-venue clause is untouched (it's a prose disposition, not tree-checkable). **Tests** (`.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.test.sh`, 5 → 11 cases, fixtures now carry real trigger sub-keys): - `branches: [release]`, `branches-ignore: [main]`, and tags-only pushes keep mcpx-nixbuild's waived main leg WAIVED and the tree green — not STALE. - `branches: [main]` in flow and block-sequence forms satisfies the leg (waiver correctly stale). - An unwaived main leg (`mcpx-fix-test-guard`) with `branches-ignore: [main]` fails as a DISAGREEMENT. - The existing 5 contract tests pass unchanged, and the checker stays green on the current-main tree with the recorded waiver set unchanged (10 waived disagreements). --- 🤖 agent-note:v1 — queue task 14311 (lane code-g). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Chores** * Improved CI policy checks to verify that main-tier workflows’ push triggers include `main`, including when branch filters are configured. * Updated validation to distinguish workflows that lack a push trigger from those whose filters exclude `main`.
